body: I believe that switching [runInTestZone](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/e748adda2e7a1f6e302628d0d76b5c3d1e3fc196/modules/angular2/src/testing/testing.ts#L129) to use `enqueueTask` instead of `setTimeout` will fix this. I'm working on a PR.

An interesting note - these exact same tests both fail (as they should) when I copy them into angular repo tests instead of the material2 repo. Maybe something to do with the different way that zone is loaded from the two karma setups? 

EDIT: I was hitting another case. I am able to repro inside the angular repo.

Hey @juliemr , it is nice to talk you, saw you solved lot of protractor issues in this forum. So I wanted to ask you about a problem similar to: "https://github.com/angular/protractor/issues/249"
and found FAQ you created regarding. I have protractor 3.0.0, trying to test AngularJS v1.3.8 app that lives in html tag seems Protractor cannot find Angular version inside angularTestResult protractor object. Since I read protractor team was about to add some special capabilities to get this working on Angular 2, wondering if this could be a possible cause of my issue?
You have any info about it?
btw: Sorry for postin' this here, other issues have been closed by you actually, so I was not sure if you would notice if I post in one of them, then I found this recent post. Thx in advance for your attention.

@Tsux please open an issue on Protractor's tracker if you feel you have found a bug, or open up a question on SO and link us there if you have a support question. It is confusing to have unrelated comments on this issue. Thank you.

Debugging this with @vicb - I think I have the same issue.
It seems that the zone when calling setTimeout is a parent of the zone when the test creates the future.
Also we observe setTimeout being called several times.

One quick option would be to kill the ngTestingZone for now and just rely completely on promises. This isn't a perfect solution (returning sub-promises can still be forgotten), but it would at least prevent silent failures from XHRs.
We've decided to go with the option above (remove ngTestingZone) until we've refactored zones completely and they cover all the XHR, rejected promise, and other cases. I am preparing a PR now.

issue.title: fix(testing): remove test zone for now and rely on returned promises
